title: Đề Thi FE PMG201c - FA25 RE (50 Câu)
description: Bộ 50 câu hỏi trắc nghiệm ôn thi PMG201c kỳ Fall 2025 Retake kèm đáp án chuẩn và phân tích chi tiết.

questions.question: True or False: A Project is defined as being unique and temporary, with a defined start and finish.
questions.explanation: A project is defined in PMBOK as a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result, with a defined start and finish.

questions.question: We discussed four types of organization structures, they are:
questions.explanation: The four main organizational structures in project management are Functional, Matrix-Based (weak, balanced, strong), Projectized (project-oriented), and Composite (hybrid).

questions.question: A project manager's primary responsibility is to deliver the product of the project within project constraints. Actions taken and changes made to the benefit of one constraint could negatively affect another. Which of the following best describes the major constraints on a project?
options: Scope, number of resources, and cost
Scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, resources, and customer satisfaction
Schedule, cost, and number of changes
questions.explanation: Modern project management recognizes competing constraints including Scope, Schedule, Cost, Quality, Risk, Resources, and Customer Satisfaction.

questions.question: The best time to assign a project manager to a project is during:
questions.explanation: A project manager should be assigned as early as possible during the Initiating process group (ideally while developing the project charter) and always before planning begins.

questions.question: An output of the Close Project or Close Phase process is the creation of:
questions.explanation: During project closure, project documentation and deliverables are indexed and archived into project archives as organizational process assets.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the development of a project charter?
options: The sponsor creates the project charter, and the project manager approves it
The project team creates the project charter, and the PMO (Project Management Office) approves it
The executive manager creates the project charter, and the functional manager approves it
The project manager creates the project charter, and the sponsor approves it
questions.explanation: The project charter is typically drafted/created by the project manager (or project initiator) and formally authorized/approved by the project sponsor.

questions.question: One of the stakeholders of the project contacts the project manager to discuss some additional scope they would like to add to the project. The project manager asks for details in writing and then works through the Control Scope process. What should the project manager do next when the evaluation of the requested scope is complete?
options: Ask the stakeholder if any more changes are expected
Make sure the impact of the change is understood by the stakeholder
Find out the root cause of why the scope was not identified during project planning
questions.explanation: Once a scope change request is evaluated, it must go through Perform Integrated Change Control for formal review and decision-making by the CCB (Change Control Board) or sponsor.

questions.question: Consider a scenario in which you learn that your project is running two weeks behind schedule. How would you know if it is acceptable to be two weeks late?
options: If the schedule baseline shows you are two weeks late, then it is not acceptable
If the team tells you the work cannot be completed any earlier than it is acceptable
Your variance thresholds should be documented in your project management plan, look there for guidance.
questions.explanation: Variance thresholds defined in the Schedule Management Plan (within the project management plan) establish predefined acceptable limits of variance before escalation or corrective actions are required.

questions.question: Which of the following action should not include in the Scope Management Plan?
options: Prepare a project scope statement based upon the project charter.
Enable the creation and maintenance of the project work breakdown structure (WBS).
Define how formal verification and acceptance of the completed project deliverables will be accomplished.
Control how requests for changes to the project scope will be processed.
Define how to identify and manage triple constraints.
questions.explanation: The Scope Management Plan defines how scope is planned, developed, managed, and controlled. Managing the overall triple constraints spans across scope, schedule, cost, and integrated project plans rather than being a specific action in the Scope Management Plan.

questions.question: True or False: An important part of the project scope statement is exclusions or out of scope items.
questions.explanation: Explicitly documenting project exclusions (what is out of scope) in the Project Scope Statement helps manage expectations and prevent scope creep.

questions.question: True or False: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is a deliverable-oriented hierarchical decomposition of the work to be executed just by the Project Manager.
questions.explanation: The WBS decomposes the total scope of work to be executed by the entire project team (not just by the Project Manager) to accomplish the project objectives and create deliverables.

questions.question: A project manager may use ______ to make sure the team members clearly know what is included in each of their work packages.
questions.explanation: The WBS Dictionary provides detailed deliverable, activity, and technical descriptions for each work package component in the WBS.

questions.question: The network diagram can be used to:
options: Control the cost performance of the project
Show project schedule performance over time
Identify opportunities to compress the project schedule
Help to justify project quality metrics
questions.explanation: Schedule network diagrams depict activity sequencing and identify the critical path, enabling project managers to spot opportunities for schedule compression (crashing or fast-tracking).

questions.question: True or False: If "develop online modules" needs to begin before "review online modules" can begin, that is called a start to start relationship.
questions.explanation: In a Start-to-Start (SS) logical relationship, a successor activity cannot start until a predecessor activity has started.

questions.question: To calculate early start (ES) of an activity which has only one predecessor, you will:
options: Take the early finish of its immediate predecessor.
Take the early start of its immediate predecessor.
Take the late finish of its immediate predecessor.
Take the late start of its immediate predecessor.
questions.explanation: During the forward pass, for an activity with a single predecessor, Early Start (ES) equals the Early Finish (EF) of that predecessor (assuming 0 lead/lag).

questions.question: Once the logic of a network is laid out, the project manager will conduct a forward pass and a backward pass through the network. This will provide information regarding ______ and will identify the ______.
options: The total duration of the project, critical path
The slack for each activity, high risk activities
The high risk activities, non-critical path
questions.explanation: A forward pass calculates early start/finish dates and the total project duration; a backward pass calculates late start/finish dates and float (slack), identifying the critical path.

questions.question: True or False: Fast Tracking is the approach to add more resources (labor, overtime, etc.) into the activities to reduce their durations.
questions.explanation: Adding resources to shorten activity duration is called 'Crashing'. 'Fast Tracking' is executing activities in parallel that were originally planned in sequence.

questions.question: A cost can be either variable or fixed. Which of the following statements are correct (choose 2 answers)?
options: Variable costs: These costs change with the amount of production. Examples include the cost of material, supplies, and wages.
Fixed costs: These costs do not change as production changes. Examples include the cost of setup, rent, utilities, etc.
Fixed costs: These costs change with the amount of production. Examples include the cost of material, supplies, and wages.
Variable costs: These costs do not change as production changes. Examples include the cost of setup, rent, utilities, etc.
questions.explanation: Variable costs vary directly with the volume of work/production (e.g., materials, supplies, wages), whereas fixed costs remain constant regardless of production volume (e.g., rent, equipment leases).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the advantages of top-down estimating?
options: Activities do not need to be identified
questions.explanation: Top-down (analogous) estimating is fast and inexpensive, but it is generally less accurate than bottom-up estimating because it is based on high-level historical analogies.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most correct statement regarding management and contingency reserves?
options: Both of them are included into the cost baseline of the project
Both of them are not included into the cost baseline of the project
Management reserve is included into the cost baseline but contingency reserve is not
Contingency reserve is included into the cost baseline but management reserve is not
questions.explanation: Contingency reserves address identified risks ('known unknowns') and are included in the cost baseline. Management reserves address unidentified risks ('unknown unknowns') and are part of the total project budget, but outside the cost baseline.

questions.question: True or False: Earned value integrates budget, quality and scope and uses monetary values to assess project status.
questions.explanation: Earned Value Management (EVM) integrates Scope, Schedule, and Cost baselines using monetary units, NOT quality.

questions.question: The discipline of quality management complements the discipline of project management. Both recognize all but one of the following:
questions.explanation: Modern quality management emphasizes Continuous Improvement (e.g. Kaizen, PDCA cycle), not one-time improvement.

questions.question: True or False: Product quality focuses on the project management processes used to meet project objectives.
questions.explanation: Product quality focuses on the features and technical conformance of the product/deliverables, whereas Process quality focuses on the project management processes.

questions.question: True or False: The Process Improvement Plan is a component of the project management plan that details how project management and development processes are to be analyzed in order to identify how to increase their value.
questions.explanation: The Process Improvement Plan details the steps for analyzing processes to identify activities that enhance their value and eliminate waste.

questions.question: True or False: Performing quality assurance within the context of a project involves taking actions to eliminate causes of unsatisfactory project performance.
questions.explanation: Quality Assurance audits quality requirements and results from quality control measurements to ensure appropriate quality standards and processes are used, taking preventive/corrective actions to eliminate causes of poor performance.

questions.question: True or False: Performing quality control within the context of a project involves applying the planned, systematic quality activities to ensure that the project correctly employs all processes needed to meet project objectives and product requirements.
questions.explanation: Applying planned, systematic quality activities to ensure processes are followed is Quality Assurance. Quality Control focuses on inspecting deliverables to ensure they meet specified requirements.

questions.question: True or False: Authority means you have the right to apply resources, make decisions and give approvals.
questions.explanation: Authority is the formal right granted to an individual to apply organizational resources, make decisions, sign approvals, and direct work.

questions.question: True or False: Project Human Resource Management includes the processes that define the tasks and assign them to suitable resources, and motivate project team to complete the tasks.
questions.explanation: Project Resource Management includes the processes that organize, manage, assign, lead, and motivate the project team.

questions.question: Which one of these should be the view of conflict?
questions.explanation: In contemporary project management, conflict is seen as inevitable and often beneficial when managed constructively, leading to better solutions and creativity.

questions.question: Which one of these is an example of role conflict:
options: When a team member does not know why he or she should do something.
When a team member does not know how to do his or her job.
When two team members are trying to complete the same task.
When a team member is late completing a task.
questions.explanation: Role conflict arises when role assignments overlap or are ambiguous, such as two team members attempting to complete the same task.

questions.question: Which one of these is not the major source of conflict that a project manager may influence?
questions.explanation: The primary sources of project conflict are schedules, project priorities, and resources. 'Project management' is not categorized as a primary source of conflict.

questions.question: Which one of these is not the approaches to conflict discussed in the Project Human Resources Management Lesson?
questions.explanation: The five recognized conflict resolution techniques are Confronting (Collaborating), Compromising, Smoothing (Accommodating), Forcing (Directing), and Avoiding (Withdrawing). 'Uninteresting' is not a conflict resolution approach.

questions.question: When you use the RACI or Responsible, Accountable, Consult, Inform version of the RAM, those informed persons are:
options: Being kept updated about project progress
questions.explanation: In a RACI matrix, 'Informed' persons are kept up-to-date on progress and decisions, typically via one-way communication.

questions.question: True or False: A project manager spends most of his/her time communicating.
questions.explanation: Project managers spend the vast majority of their time (estimated at 75% to 90%) communicating with stakeholders, team members, and sponsors.

questions.question: Which item would most likely NOT be part of a basic communication plan:
options: The amount of their annual bonus
The best medium for the communication
questions.explanation: A communication management plan describes stakeholder communication requirements, frequency, and channels, but does not include confidential individual compensation or bonus figures.

questions.question: Upward communication is communication to/from:
questions.explanation: Upward communication flows vertically from the project manager/team up to senior management, executives, or sponsors.

questions.question:
Which one is the correct matching of communication methods and the explanations?
Communication methods:
(1) Interactive
(2) Push
(3) Pull
Explanations:
(a) Between two or more parties and multidirectional; the most efficient way to ensure common understanding.
(b) Sent to recipients; does not ensure it was actually received and understood.
(c) Recipients must access the information; works for large amounts of information or large audiences, each recipient accesses at their own discretion.
questions.explanation: (1) Interactive corresponds to (a) multidirectional exchange. (2) Push corresponds to (b) sent directly to recipients. (3) Pull corresponds to (c) accessed by recipients at their discretion.

questions.question: During status review meetings to evaluate project performance and progress, which report is NOT preferred to use?
questions.explanation: Status review meetings focus on macro progress, variance, and forecast metrics (Status, Progress, and Forecasting reports). Detailed test reports are specialized technical documents rather than high-level status review instruments.

questions.question: The purpose of project risk management is to:
options: Minimize the likelihood or the impact of negative events or threats to your project and to increase the likelihood or impact of positive events
Neutralize the likelihood or the impact of negative events or threats to your project and to neutralize the likelihood or impact of positive events
Minimize the likelihood or the impact of positive events or threats to your project and to increase the likelihood or impact of negative events
Eliminate the likelihood or the impact of negative events or threats to your project and to decrease the likelihood or impact of positive events
questions.explanation: Project Risk Management aims to increase the probability and/or impact of positive events (opportunities) and reduce the probability and/or impact of adverse events (threats).

questions.question: True or False: The primary output from the identification of risks is the stakeholder register.
questions.explanation: The primary output of the Identify Risks process is the Risk Register (and Risk Report), not the stakeholder register.

questions.question: If the response you choose is to avoid a risk this means that:
options: You simply do not consider the risk.
You change your plans so that you eliminate the risk.
You note the risk but do not talk about it.
questions.explanation: Risk avoidance is a risk response strategy whereby the project team alters the project management plan to completely eliminate the threat or isolate the project from its impact.

questions.question: True or False: During a risk brainstorming session, a team member identifies a risk. This particular risk does not seem to belong to any of the categories in your Risk Breakdown Structure (RBS). You thank him for his work, but inform him that the risk cannot be included because it does not fit any of the categories defined in the RBS.
questions.explanation: An RBS is a framework to assist in identifying risks, not a restrictive filter to ignore valid project risks. If a legitimate risk is identified, it must be recorded in the risk register and the RBS should be updated.

questions.question: True or False: If you are not certain who your stakeholders are, asking who will use the product or service being created can be helpful.
questions.explanation: End users and beneficiaries are essential stakeholders. Identifying who will use or be impacted by the deliverables is a fundamental stakeholder identification practice.

questions.question: If a stakeholder has high interest and high power then as the project manager you:
options: Can try to move them to be low interest and low power so that they do not take up too much of your time.
Can try to move them to be high interest and low power so they do not get in your way.
Focus your time and attention on them, they are very impactful to your project and you want to keep them engaged and positive.
Can ignore them, they are as you need them to be.
questions.explanation: On the Power/Interest Grid, stakeholders with high power and high interest fall into the 'Manage Closely' quadrant, requiring focused time and proactive engagement.

questions.question: You just came from a meeting with one of your project stakeholders; he knew about your project and was not against it, but did not seem to be particularly interested in it either. How would you classify him?
questions.explanation: A neutral stakeholder is aware of the project and its potential outcomes but is neither supportive nor resistant.

questions.question: True or False: The Project Sponsor is responsible for stakeholder expectations management.
questions.explanation: Managing stakeholder expectations and engagement is the direct responsibility of the Project Manager.

questions.question: Your stakeholder register is your primary output and should at least contain:
options: Job descriptions, identification information, and stakeholder classification
Assessment information, scope information, and stakeholder classification
Assessment information, identification information, and stakeholder classification
Assessment information, identification information, and risk classification
questions.explanation: A Stakeholder Register primarily contains three sections: Identification information, Assessment information, and Stakeholder classification.

questions.question: The team is helping the project manager to estimate activities on their project. There are several activities they need to estimate that have not been previously done by the company. What is the best method of estimating these activities?
questions.explanation: When activities carry high uncertainty or lack historical data, Three-Point Estimating (PERT: Optimistic, Most Likely, Pessimistic) is the best technique to account for estimation risk.

questions.question:
You have a project to build a new fence. The fence will form a square. Each side is to take one day to build, and $1,000 has been budgeted per side. The sides are planned to be completed one after the other. Today is the end of day 3. Using the following project status chart to calculate project current EV:
- Side 1: Complete, spent $1,000
- Side 2: Complete, spent $900
- Side 3: 50% done, spent $600
- Side 4: 75% done, spent $600
In Earned Value Management Technique, you can compute the Schedule Variance (SV) by applying which of following formula?
questions.explanation: Schedule Variance formula is SV = EV - PV (Earned Value minus Planned Value). SV > 0 means ahead of schedule; SV < 0 means behind schedule.
